Man Buys New 2023 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 for $124,375, Drives 5K Miles, Sells for $92,500
18 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Even though you can do better in terms of specs, I believe this Z06 Coupe still represents tremendous value for money, but that's only if you're happy with the Elkhart Lake Blue Metallic colorway and the Sky Cool Gray interior. Otherwise, it's probably worth it to spend a few extra grand and just get a Z06 in whatever color you want, since a good wrap will cost you about $5k anyway.
I don't know if it's just me, but I don't really like the C8 in blue. I find this difficult to explain, because blue is one of my favorite colors. I guess there's just something about this particular shade. It's a medium-to-deep metallic blue that's meant to strike a balance between emphasizing the car's design and still being sufficiently reflective under direct sunlight.
To me it looks as though it's "neither here nor there". Maybe it's because I clearly prefer a more traditional dark navy metallic color, and a lighter shade of blue feels like it's not serious enough - nor is it vibrant enough to keep up with a bright red or yellow. Maybe it's also the C8's overall design. Some of its lines seem to dissipate under this so-called balance between dark and reflective. I feel like I've overdone the colors thing. Sorry.
Anyway, regarding this car, it was purchased new for $124,375 by the same person who decided to auction it off after driving it just over 5,000 miles. The winning bid came in at $92,500, plus a buyer's fee. Look, if you don't mind the color, this is amazing value for money. The new owner should be delighted.
Am I exaggerating? Not at all. Take a look at this 2024 Corvette Z06 Coupe 1LZ in Torch Red. It sold for $91,500 with 11,000 miles on the clock. Again, a 1LZ, not a 2LZ. And with twice as many miles on the odometer. Pretty much the same price.
Aside from the Elkhart Lake Blue exterior, this Z06 also comes with a rear spoiler, LED headlights, tinted windows, chrome rear badging, rear parking sensors, plus a set of 20" and 21" forged wheels with Michelin tires and yellow-finished calipers. There's also a front-axle lift system, to go with Magnetic Selective Ride Control.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the power-adjustable GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilated), a Bose sound system, head-up display, a heated leather-wrapped steering wheel, a performance data recorder, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, sat-nav, and more. I don't mind the spec, even though there are some blemishes on the left door panel and right-side lower trim. It's not a brand-new car, but it's still a whole lot of car for a little over $90k.
What really "sells" the Z06 is the 5.5-liter LT6 V8 engine, pushing out 670 horsepower and 460 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets routed to the rear wheels via a Tremec TR-9080 eight-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox, allowing you to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill in just 2.6 seconds (with a 1-foot rollout), before maxing out at 195 mph (314 kph).
